y1: The Pharisees and Sadducees were actually enemies, but they came together to test Jesus. Jesus says, 'You know how to discern the appearance of the sky, but you can't discern the signs of the times,' and tells them He will only give them the sign of Jonah.
y2: The disciples were worried because they forgot the bread. Jesus says, 'You of little faith,' and reminds them of two miracles. The real danger was not hunger, but their yeast, that is, their teaching.
y3: Even though the disciples saw the miracle twice, they still worried. Faith grows more by 'remembering' the grace we have already received than by new miracles. Jesus asks, 'Don't you remember?'
y5: Caesarea Philippi was a pagan city with a temple to the god Pan and a temple to the emperor on a huge rock cliff. In that place where gods and the emperor competed, Jesus asks, 'But who do you say I am?'
y6: Peter's answer: 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.' Jesus says, 'You are Peter. On this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades will not overcome it,' and He gives him the keys to the kingdom of heaven.
y7: There is a play on words between 'Peter' (Petros) and 'rock' (petra). Church traditions interpret differently whether the rock is Peter himself or his confession. What is clear is that the church is built on the confession 'Jesus is the Christ,' through the people who make this confession.
y9: 'From that time on,' Jesus openly says for the first time that He will suffer, die, and rise again in Jerusalem. This is the second turning point in the Gospel of Matthew, pairing with the 'From that time on' in.
y10: Peter, who had just been praised, took hold of Jesus and objected. Jesus rebukes him, 'Get behind Me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to Me.' The rock suddenly turned into a stumbling block. A Messiah without a cross was the path Satan offered in the wilderness ().
y11: Peter's words came out of love. But even good intentions can hinder God's will. Confessing Jesus as the 'Christ' and accepting 'what kind of Christ' He is are different things.
y13: 'If anyone desires to come after Me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow Me.' The cross was a Roman tool of execution. The condemned carried their own cross to the place of execution.
y14: 'For what will it profit a person if he gains the whole world, and forfeits his life?' It is a paradox. Whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses it for Jesus will find it.
y15: Self-denial is not hating oneself, but handing over the steering wheel of life to Jesus. It is not throwing away 'me', but throwing away 'the life where I am the master'.
verse: “He said to them, 'But who do you say that I am?' Simon Peter answered, 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.'”
prayer: Lord, You are the Christ, the Son of the living God. Let me build my life on this confession. Let me think not about the things of men, but the things of God, hand over my steering wheel to You, take up my cross, and follow You. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
d0: yeast. In it represents the growth of God's Kingdom, but here it means the spread of false teaching. It is small, but it spreads through everything. 'A little yeast leavens the whole lump' ().
d1: Christ. In the Old Testament, kings, priests, and prophets were anointed. 'The Anointed One' is the King from the line of David promised by God. The Gospel of Matthew begins with the words, 'The genealogy of Jesus Christ'.
d2: Peter. His real name was Simon. Jesus gave him the name 'stone'. Even though his character was unstable, Jesus turned him into a rock. In Azerbaijani, it is called 'Peter'.
d3: deny oneself. The same verb is used when Peter 'denies' Jesus in chapter 26. We either deny Jesus, or we deny ourselves. 'Let him deny himself' (16:24) and 'You will deny Me three times' (26:34).
